facts.statement: The only known species, Q. henanensis, has a specific epithet named after the province of Henan.
facts.quote: The genus contains a single species, Q. henanensis, the specific epithet for which was named for the province of Henan.

facts.statement: Qiupalong was described in 2011 by a team of scientists from China, South Korea, Japan, and Canada led by Li Xu.
facts.quote: It was described in 2011 by a team of scientists from various institutions in China, South Korea, Japan, and Canada which included Li Xu, Yoshitsugu Kobayashi, Junchang Lü, Yuong-Nam Lee, Yongqing Liu, Kohei Tanaka, Xingliao Zhang, Songhai Jia, and Jiming Zhang.

facts.statement: The holotype is a partial postcranial skeleton designated HGM 41HIII-0106 and is housed in the Henan Geological Museum.
facts.quote: The holotype consists of a partial postcranial skeleton and is housed in the Henan Geological Museum and was given the designation HGM 41HIII-0106.

facts.statement: In 2017, researchers including Philip J. Currie described postcranial ornithomimid remains from the Belly River Group in Alberta, Canada.
facts.quote: In 2017, another team of researchers including Philip J. Currie, described some postcranial ornithomimid remains from the Belly River Group in Alberta, Canada.

facts.statement: Specimens from Alberta were referred to the genus Qiupalong due to significant morphological similarities to the holotype.
facts.quote: When these newer specimens were described, the authors noted that they bore significant morphological similarities to the holotype of Qiupalong.

facts.statement: The referral of Alberta specimens made Qiupalong the only ornithomimid genus known from both Asia and Laramidia.
facts.quote: This would also make Qiupalong the only genus of ornithomimid known from both Asia and Laramidia.

facts.statement: In 2023, Alexander Averianov and colleagues described a juvenile ornithomimosaur tibia from the Udurchukan Formation in the Russian Far East.
facts.quote: In 2023, the tibia of a juvenile ornithomimosaur from the Udurchukan Formation of the Amur Oblast in the Russian Far East was described by Alexander Averianov and colleagues.

facts.statement: The Qiupa Formation dates to the end of the Maastrichtian stage, the final stage of the Mesozoic Era.
facts.quote: More specific analyses have suggested that the formation dates to the end of the Maastrichtian stage, which was the final stage of the Mesozoic Era.

facts.statement: Rubén Molina-Pérez and Asier Larramendi estimated Qiupalong's length at 2.85 m and its mass at 63 kg.
facts.quote: They did not give an estimate for the animal's overall size, but Rubén Molina-Pérez and Asier Larramendi suggested a length of 2.85 m and a mass of 63 kg.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of several disarticulated postcranial bones.
facts.quote: The holotype of Qiupalong, given the designation HGM 41HIII-0106, consists of several disarticulated bones from the postcranial skeleton.

facts.statement: Qiupalong has downward-curved toe claws resembling basal ornithomimosaurs, unlike other derived Asian ornithomimids.
facts.quote: The toe claws are curved downwards, which resembles the condition seen in basal ornithomimosaurs and is unlike other derived ornithomimids from Asia.

facts.statement: Qiupalong's metatarsals display the arctometatarsalian condition, similar to Ornithomimus, Struthiomimus, and Gallimimus.
facts.quote: The metatarsals display the arctometatarsalian condition, and they are almost identical to the other derived ornithomimids including Ornithomimus, Struthiomimus, and Gallimimus.

facts.statement: The shape of Qiupalong's pubis is more similar to North American ornithomimids than to non-ornithomimid ornithomimosaurs like Shenzhousaurus and Harpymimus.
facts.quote: The shape of the pubis is also more similar to ornithomimids from North America than it is to non-ornithomimid ornithomimosaurs like Shenzhousaurus and Harpymimus.

facts.statement: Qiupalong is classified as an extinct genus of ornithomimosaurian theropod.
facts.quote: Qiupalong (IPA: ; ) is an extinct genus of ornithomimosaurian theropod

facts.statement: Researchers did not refer the Russian Far East remains to any specific genus within Ornithomimidae.
facts.quote: However, Averianov and colleagues did not refer the remains to any specific genus within Ornithomimidae.

facts.statement: In 2017, researchers led by Bradly McFeeters assigned several previously unassigned ornithomimosaur specimens to the genus Qiupalong.
facts.quote: In 2017, a team of authors led by Bradly McFeeters revisited these specimens and referred several of them to the recently described genus, Qiupalong.

facts.statement: The initial Qiupalong specimens referred to the genus included vertebrae, ribs, limb bones, hip bones, an ankle bone, and a pedal claw.
facts.quote: These specimens included CMN 8902 (vertebrae, ribs, scapulocoracoid, partial limb bones, and hip bones), UALVP 53595 (an ankle bone), UALVP 52861 (pedal ungual).

facts.statement: Specimens referred to Qiupalong sp. were not diagnostic enough for a specific species but strongly resembled bones from the holotype of Qiupalong henanensis.
facts.quote: These specimens were referred to Qiupalong sp. because they were not diagnostic to the species level, but they strongly resembled some of the bones of the holotype of Q. henanensis.

facts.statement: Histological analysis of a juvenile Qiupalong-like tibia suggests the individual was a young adult still actively growing when it died.
facts.quote: Averianov and colleagues suggested, based on the presence of active secondary remodeling and the lack of an external fundamental system, that the individual was a young adult which was still actively growing when it died.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses place Qiupalong in a clade with Struthiomimus and Ornithomimus, known as the "North American clade".
facts.quote: They recovered Qiupalong in a clade with Struthiomimus and Ornithomimus, which they refer to as the "North American clade" (after Kobiyashi and Lü who recovered the same clade).

facts.statement: The "North American clade" containing Qiupalong is characterized by an acute angle between the pubic shaft and boot and an anterior extension of the pubic boot tip.
facts.quote: This clade is diagnosed by a very acute angle between pubic shaft and boot and a tip of anterior extension of the pubic boot.

facts.statement: Some phylogenetic analyses, such as those by Averianov and Dieter-Sues, have recovered slightly different evolutionary positions for Qiupalong compared to other studies.
facts.quote: Averianov and Dieter-Sues recovered a slightly different phylogeny using the data set produced by Jonah Choiniere and colleagues in 2012.

facts.statement: Although the skull of Qiupalong is unknown, it is assumed to have been edentulous with a beak, similar to other ornithomimids.
facts.quote: The skull of Qiupalong is not known, although it is assumed that it was likely similar to other ornithomimids in being edentulous and having a beak.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Qiupalong likely had a diet similar to Ornithomimus and Struthiomimus and may have coexisted with them with minimal competition.
facts.quote: Cullen and colleagues suggested that it probably had a similar diet to other ornithomimids like Ornithomimus and Struthiomimus and may have even coexisted alongside them with minimal competition.

facts.statement: Despite the first described Qiupalong remains coming from Asia, the geologically oldest fossils of the genus are from Laramidia (North America).
facts.quote: Although the first remains of Qiupalong to be described were from Asia, the geologically oldest remains from the genus are from Laramidia.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Qiupalong originated in North America and migrated to Asia near the very end of the Cretaceous Period.
facts.quote: This, coupled with the results of several phylogenetic analyses, suggest that Qiupalong originated in North America and only migrated into Asia later, near the very end of the Cretaceous Period.

facts.statement: The exact timing of Qiupalong's migration to Asia remains uncertain due to less thorough geochronological study of Cretaceous Asia compared to North America.
facts.quote: The exact time that this migration occurred is uncertain because the geochronology of Cretaceous Asia has not been studied as thoroughly as the geochronology of North America.

facts.statement: Qiupalong fossils were found in bed 34 of the Qiupa Formation, an intermediate-age layer that yielded the majority of the formation's dinosaur body fossils.
facts.quote: Qiupalong was found in "bed 34", which is intermediate in age relative to the sediments of the formation as a whole and is the locality from which a majority of the formation's dinosaur body fossils have been recovered.

facts.statement: The environment where Qiupalong fossils were deposited was a braided river delta.
facts.quote: This sedimentary layer would have been deposited by a braided river delta that created the depositional environment necessary for fossils to form.

facts.statement: Qiupalong lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The earliest fossils of Qiupalong come from the Oldman Formation or the Dinosaur Park Formation.
facts.quote: The earliest record of Qiupalong is from either the Oldman Formation or the Dinosaur Park Formation.

facts.statement: Most confidently assigned Qiupalong remains are found in the lower half of the Dinosaur Park Formation, approximately 20 meters above the contact with the Oldman Formation.

facts.statement: Qiupalong likely coexisted with the ornithomimids Ornithomimus and possibly Struthiomimus.
facts.quote: Qiupalong is believed to have coexisted with Ornithomimus and possibly also Struthiomimus.

facts.statement: Researchers hypothesize that Qiupalong may have formed multi-species assemblages similar to modern African bovids.
facts.quote: It has also been hypothesized that they may have formed multi-species assemblages, analogous to bovids in Africa today.

facts.statement: Qiupalong likely coexisted with three known caenagnathids: Citipes, Chirostenotes, and Caenagnathus.
facts.quote: Qiupalong also likely coexisted with the three known caenagnathids from the area, Citipes, Chirostenotes, and Caenagnathus.

facts.quote: Parent group: Ornithomimidae
